questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was in the EU and has great skiing options.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Super easy. ETH provided all the necessary information that one needed upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all they send a lot of emails with practical informations. And then, on the first day of the semester there was a info-lecture for exchangestudents, that told everything one needed for insurance, residence permit etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: ETH has an option to do an actual exchange of accomodations - so I just swapped my appartment with a local student going to Copenhagen the same semester. A very good experience.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: eLINK! All students almost live off Campus, besides the university has multiple campi accross the city. So although I basically lived "on campus", all my lectures and excersices where on the other side of town. Luckily ETH provides fast and frequent shuttlebusses between campi, so as long as you live close to one, you can easily get around (for free). Besides, public transport in Zurich is super good, so almost no matter where you live it will be easy to get around and get to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
For biology one signs up for "block courses" a month before semesterstart. Here it is important to choose a lot of courses, as there is a big chance not to get ones first priorities due to limitid places. (ETH sends an email about this).

One signs up for courses at a designated webpage - myStudies - at the semester start. Normally students take way to many courses the first week, just to try them out, and decide what to spend the semester on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: ETH send e-mails during the procces to guide one through.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesfull. I think I got 50% of the courses I initially wanted, but all my courses turned out to be very interesting - so I'm not sad about this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out a lot of courses, and dont be affraid to take courses from other departments. To easen the academic burden, it can also be smart to take one or two "guest courses", which are considered to be way easier than the normal ETH courses. I took the guest course "Technology Entrepeneurship", which I dont think was that intersting, but it gave me some slack to focus on some of my more challenging courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 30 ECTS of BA level courses and 6 ECTS of MA level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less homework, and more time in the lab/classroom at ETH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

"Immunology 1"
"Population and Quantitative Genetics"
"Technology Entrepeneurship"
Crashcourse at ETH/UZH sprachenzentrum "Deutch A1.1"
LTK Module 1

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
"Mass spec for proteomics" 9/10 - fun course with both wet and dry lab. The people teaching this course are also pioneers in the field, which was very inspirering. And it gave some nice experience with omics-analysis in R, without requirering any R knowledge.
"Biophysics of Microtubule Cytoskeleton" 7/10. Very easy block course but we didnt do that much. Nice to get some more freetime to explore switzerland.
"Insulin Signaling" 7/10. But I learned how to do all the basic methods (WB, qPCR, cellculture and immaging etc.). I learned a lot, but the workdays were loooong.
"Parallels between Tissue Repair and Cancer". Actually a very nice course. Cool that one got to make ones own research project in the last week.
"Immunology 1" 6/10 Just lectures. It was so so.
"Population and Quantitative Genetics" 9/10 - this was just great! Not too difficult, but very interesting.
"Technology Entrepeneurship" 4/10. Easy.
Crashcourse at ETH/UZH sprachenzentrum "Deutch A1.1" 10/10. This is a must as an exchange student. You get a lot of new friends, and are able to talk german with your lab-mates later in the semester.

questions.answer: Prices are very similar to danish prices - just eating out seemed more expensive to me. Also, I have heard that meat is more expensive, but I dont buy that myself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In ASVZ you get the chance to try every sport, and attend really good classes/lessons (look it up - it's amazing!!!) and it's free for all exchange students. Besides there are a lot of social clubs at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ASVZ!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on hikes!! There are so many beautiful places to see. You can start with: Murren, Creux de Van, Stoos and Pizol five Lakes. Use this for off-line maps:
https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/hiking-maps
. Every kanton has a touris guide with great hikes:)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Swiss culture is very special, but in terms of social norms it is quite simillar to danish (introverted culture).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take small courses - either lab or seminar courses. ASVZ. Try to speak german with them - they like this:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is expected that you put more hours into your schoolwork than a lot of other places, and many students are very "locked in".

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature appreciation, most students will go on hikes or skiing in the weekends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open and do things. Remember to go for all the experiences you can. It keeps you busy so you dont think about home to much, and will give you some amazing experiences.
2. Relax about school, and remember you are on exchange. There is possibility to take so many incredible courses, but make sure to take some that are also just easy, so you have time to do other things than studying.
3. Please try new style hustle in the ASVZ (Danni).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing friends I got:)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: LTK M1

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
